detail.title: x - Local Authorities with less than 5 pupils or a percentage based on less than 5 pupils or an allocation amount based on less than 5 pupils for Service Child Pupil Premium, LAC or Post LAC have had their figures suppressed for data protection.
Data includes Academies and Free Schools as at 01/06/@year1.
Mainstream Schools include Mainstream Academies, Free Schools and City Technology Colleges (CTC).
Pupil numbers in Pupil Referral Units (PRU) and Alternative Provision (AP) academies which were formerly PRUs are based on January @year1 school census data.

Deprivation pupil numbers are full time equivalent (FTE) number of pupils aged 4 and over as at 31 August @year0 in Reception to Year 11 (pupils aged 4 to 15 where National Curriculum year groups do not apply), as recorded on the October @year0 School Census who are known to have been eligible for Free School Meals (FSM) in the previous six years. FSM eligibility in the previous six years will be determined by those pupils recorded on the October @year0 School Census who were recorded as known to be eligible for FSM on the School Census since Spring 2017, known as Ever 6. FTEs are calculated on the same basis as the Dedicated Schools Grant.

Post Looked after Children are Full time equivalent (FTE) number of pupils aged 4 and over as at 31 August @year0 in Reception to Year 11 (pupils aged 4 to 15 where National Curriculum year groups do not apply) as recorded on the October @year0 School Census who are known to be adopted from care, or are ceased to be looked after through a child arrangement order or who leave care under a special guardianship order or residence order.

Looked after Children (LAC) include children aged 4 to 15 (at 31 August @year0) who have been looked after for at least 1 day in the year ending 31 March @year1. This excludes children whose only episode(s) of care during the year was as a result of respite, or were on remand/committed for trial or sentence and accommodated by the local authority. This data has been collected from the @year-1-@year0short Looked After Children Return from local authorities (SSDA903). In December @year1 we will update using LAC data from the @year0 to @year1 SDA903 (March @year1).
Primary pupils include pupils in National Curriculum year groups Reception to 6 and pupils not following the National Curriculum aged 4 to 10 as at August @year0.
Secondary pupils include pupils in National Curriculum year groups 7 to 11 and pupils not following the National Curriculum aged 11 to 15 as at August @year0.

Each primary FSM Ever 6 eligible pupil will attract @britishCurrencySymbol1,455 through the Pupil Premium. For pupils in maintained primary schools, maintained secondary schools, maintained special schools and non-maintained special schools (NMSS), funding will be passed on via the local authorities. For pupils in academies and special academies, the ESFA will pass funding directly to the setting.

Each secondary FSM Ever 6 eligible pupil will attract @britishCurrencySymbol1,035 through the Pupil Premium. For pupils in maintained primary schools, maintained secondary schools, maintained special schools and NMSS, funding will be passed on via the local authorities. For pupils in academies and special academies, the ESFA will pass funding directly to the setting.

Each pupil adopted from care, those who leave care under a special guardianship order or residence order will attract @britishCurrencySymbol2,530 through the Pupil Premium Plus. For pupils in maintained primary schools, maintained secondary schools, maintained special schools and NMSS, funding will be passed on via the local authorities. For pupils in academies and special academies, the ESFA will pass funding directly to the setting.

Each Looked After Child will attract @britishCurrencySymbol2,530 through the Pupil Premium Plus and the funding for all looked after children will be allocated via the local authority's Virtual School Head. Allocations are based on @year0-@year1short SSDA903 data (till March @year1), but the funding may be used by Virtual School Heads to provide support for any child who is looked after for one day or more during the @year-1-@year0short financial year.

Each Post-LAC or Looked After Child will attract @britishCurrencySymbol2,530 through the Pupil Premium Plus. However, they will not be eligible to also receive the Deprivation element of Pupil Premium, regardless of whether they are also flagged as an FSM Ever 6 eligible pupil. Therefore, these allocations include the removal of FSM Ever 6 funding for pupils identified as being a Post-LAC or Looked After Child.
Data includes General hospital schools based on the January @year1 SLASC data.
